newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.

text.p: Bids for U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Wednesday of $62.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $63.00, steady with Tuesday's active sales, feedlot sources said.
"They bought some at $63.00 yesterday and then pulled back the bid some, but I think we'll see more trade at $63.00 today," a Texas Panhandle-area source said.

About 40,000 head sold Tuesday in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week-to-date figure near 72,000, sources said. An estimated 40,000 to 45,000 head sold in Kansas, with a weekly number close to 60,000.

Cattle bought Tuesday were destined for pick-ups early next week so that packers would have enough animals to start operations following the three-day Independence Day holiday weekend, feedlot sources said.
However, some of the cattle reportedly will be delivered for Thursday or Saturday operations, they said.
Most major packers will be closed on Friday in observance of the holiday, but a few small cow plants could be open, the sources said.
